sentences.text: The known remains include an upper arm bone measuring 110 cm and a forearm bone reaching 69 cm in length.
Paleontologist Octávio Mateus found the fossil on May 25 near Iembe in the Bengo province.
The genus was officially described by Mateus and his team in 2011.
Modern phylogenetic tests place Angolatitan as a non-titanosaurian titanosauriform.
This basal titanosauriform lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically between 89.8 and 85.7 million years ago during the Coniacian stage.
The ecosystem it inhabited was likely a desert-like environment.
More precise dating places the animal between 89.8 and 85.7 million years ago during the Coniacian stage.
